evidence_note: One MCP shot with the video measured directly. The MCP supplied the descriptive schema (confidence 0.95); every number below is MEASURED off 60fps frames because the MCP's `animation` is derived from the labels timing:medium + springiness:subtle, not from the footage. §5 checklist answered in each PATTERN.md; 1, 3 and 4 pass for all three.
animation: MEASURED per pattern — the mark→caret morph is .spring(response: 0.135, dampingFraction: 1.00) -> { mass: 1, stiffness: 2162, damping: 93 }. The MCP reported .spring(0.45, 0.72) for the whole shot, which is its label-derived default and matches nothing measured here.

measured.note: Read off 60fps frames. Screen rect inside the mockup: 406x879+337+100 (auto-detected).
measured.mark_to_caret_morph: onset ~292ms, settle ~470ms (~200ms). Bounding box of the white glyph goes 70x86 -> 5x48: NON-UNIFORM, width collapses to 7% while height only reaches 56%. Fitted zeta=1.00 w0=46.5 (rms 0.0151), beating iOS-standard/140ms (0.0236) and easeOut/100ms (0.0340). No overshoot at any frame.
measured.batch_swap: The card set is REPLACED wholesale roughly every 2.4s (5 phrases across 12.3s). Quadrant luminance shows the four regions changing 100-150ms apart, i.e. a staggered swap, not a scroll.
measured.word_roll: The trailing word changes over ~250ms (8583 -> 8833ms), travelling vertically through a 54px band while the previous word fades — a roll, not typing.
measured.no_vertical_scroll: Phase correlation over a 260x600 card column at lags of 100/200/500ms returns 0-2px of vertical displacement while RMSE grows 0.059->0.122. The cards change WITHOUT translating: they do not scroll.
mcp_divergences: start_state: the MCP calls the initial glyph 'a white vertical bar representing the logo mark'. It is a BOOKMARK glyph that morphs INTO the bar; the bar is the text caret. The bookmark exists for only ~375ms and the MCP's keyframes are 1s apart, so it never saw it.
'an array of image cards scrolls through the screen background' — measured: no vertical translation at all. The batch is swapped in place.
motion_behavior includes 'typing' and the prose says 'typewriter-style text updates'. Measured: the word rolls vertically and crossfades. No character-by-character reveal.

description.one_line_summary: A brand mark contracts into the blinking caret of a search field, which then cycles categories while a gallery of cards swaps behind it.
description.detailed_description: A bookmark-shaped brand mark sits centred on black. It contracts — fast and completely dry — until it IS the blinking text caret of an empty search field. The caret blinks alone for about 2.5s, then a search prompt appears beside it with a small gradient thumbnail. For the next 12s the prompt cycles through categories: the trailing word rolls vertically to the next one while, behind it, the whole set of gallery cards is replaced by a new set, the four quadrants swapping 100-150ms apart. At the end the cards clear and the field contracts back into the mark.

motion_breakdown.start_state: A bookmark-shaped white mark centred on a pitch-black screen. Nothing else is on screen.
motion_breakdown.transition: The mark contracts non-uniformly — width to 7%, height to 56% — over ~200ms on a critically damped spring, arriving as the caret of an empty search field. It blinks; the prompt and a gradient thumbnail join it; then the trailing word rolls to the next category every ~2.4s while the card set behind swaps in staggered quadrants.
motion_breakdown.end_state: Cards cleared, field contracted, the bookmark mark alone on black again.
motion_breakdown.why_it_works: The mark does not fade into the field, it BECOMES the part of it that matters — the caret, the thing that says 'type here'. Identity is spent buying the affordance instead of being replaced by it. It is critically damped for the same reason: a caret that overshoots reads as a glitch, because a text cursor is the one element a user expects to be perfectly still.

description.confidence_note: High for the morph: 45 frames at 60fps, a curve fit beating every easing tried, and a clean non-uniform scale read off the glyph's bounding box. Lower for the two showcase patterns — the batch cadence and the 100-150ms quadrant stagger come from luminance sampling rather than from tracking individual cards, and the word roll is timed to +/-1 frame but its easing was not fitted. Deliberately BELOW the MCP's own 0.95, because three of its descriptive claims did not survive measurement.
